rows.name: Self-taught + guesses
rows.author: Essam Gouda
rows.description: Self-taught + look-ahead with a second model of its own that guesses who holds each hidden card. It learned those guesses only from its own games, and imagines many more hands from them.
method: the model keeps its top 2 cards
imagine 256 hands from where its guess model thinks the cards are
try each card: the model plays out the round
play the card with the best average score

rows.name: Kooz bot
rows.author: Abdulrahman Boudi
rows.description: Look-ahead on models trained from scratch. It imagines 64 deals from its own guess model, tries every legal card, and only makes a Dash Call when its bid model rates it clearly worth it.
method: the bid net picks the bid; a Dash Call only if it is worth +10 or more
imagine hidden hands from the guess net, keep those that fit the bids x64
each legal card: the card net plays all 4 seats to the end

rows.name: Hybrid v4
rows.author: Yosif Elessawi
rows.description: One model bids, one chooses cards, and one guesses who holds the hidden cards. It tries its top 2 cards on 32 imagined deals built from those guesses.
method: the bid model picks the bid
the card model keeps its top 2 cards
imagine 32 deals from where the guess model thinks the cards are
play each kept card to the end

rows.name: Self-taught + look-ahead
rows.author: Essam Gouda
rows.description: The Self-taught model bids alone and picks its best cards, then tries each one on imagined hands.
method: the model keeps its top 3 cards
try each card: the model plays out the round
play the card with the best average score

rows.name: Self-taught
rows.author: Essam Gouda
rows.description: One trained model makes every decision. It began by playing randomly and learned only by playing itself, with no strategy written in and nothing copied.
method: learned from millions of practice decisions
the model rates every legal move

rows.name: Hybrid with Copycat cards
rows.author: Essam Gouda
rows.description: Trained bot + look-ahead with its card model swapped for Copycat with practice. It keeps the original bidding model.
method: Trained bot's bidding model picks the bid
Copycat with practice keeps its top 3 cards
imagine hands that fit everyone's bids x16
try each card: the card model plays out the round
play the card with the best average score

rows.name: Trained bot + look-ahead
rows.author: Yosif Elessawi
rows.description: Trained bot's models choose which cards are worth considering. It then tries each one on imagined hands.
method: card model keeps its top 3 cards
imagine hands that fit everyone's bids x16
try each card: the models play out the round
play the card with the best average score

rows.name: Copycat with practice + look-ahead
rows.author: Essam Gouda
rows.description: The practised model picks its 2 best cards, then Look-ahead tries them on imagined hands.
method: bid the tricks the hand should win
card model keeps its top 2 cards
try each card: Basic rules plays out the round
play the card with the best average score

rows.name: Copycat with practice
rows.author: Essam Gouda
rows.description: Copycat's model, improved further by playing itself. It bids with Basic rules.
method: bid the tricks the hand should win
card model rates every legal card

rows.name: Trained bot
rows.author: Yosif Elessawi
rows.description: Two trained models, one for bidding and one for cards. It started by copying Look-ahead, then improved by playing itself.
method: learned from thousands of practice games
card model rates every legal card

rows.name: Copycat
rows.author: Essam Gouda
rows.description: A trained model that learned its card play by copying Look-ahead. It bids with Basic rules and does no look-ahead itself.
method: bid the tricks the hand should win
card model rates every legal card

rows.name: Copycat + look-ahead
rows.author: Essam Gouda
rows.description: Copycat's model picks the most promising cards, so Look-ahead can spend its effort trying only those.
method: bid the tricks the hand should win
card model keeps its top 3 cards
try each card: Basic rules plays out the round
play the card with the best average score

rows.name: Look-ahead
rows.author: Yosif Elessawi
rows.description: Imagines what the others might hold, plays each card to the end of the round using Basic rules, and picks what scored best.
method: bid the tricks the hand should win
try each card: Basic rules plays out the round
play the card with the best average score

rows.name: Look-ahead, tuned rules
rows.author: Yosif Elessawi
rows.description: Like Look-ahead, but it plays each card out with rules tuned for that job.
method: bid the tricks the hand should win
try each card: a tuned rule plays out the round
play the card with the best average score

rows.name: Cautious rules
rows.author: Essam Gouda
rows.description: Basic rules, set to take fewer risks.
method: bid the tricks the hand should win
last to call? avoid the risky number
still need tricks? win cheaply, else throw low

rows.name: Always highest card
rows.author: Essam Gouda
rows.description: A simple example bot. It never bids and always plays its highest card.

rows.name: Always lowest card
rows.author: Essam Gouda
rows.description: A simple example bot. It never bids and always plays its lowest card.

rows.name: Rules + trump count
rows.author: Essam Gouda
rows.description: Basic rules, except it stops chasing tricks once its unbeatable trumps cover what it still needs.
method: bid the tricks the hand should win
count my trumps nobody can beat
they cover the tricks I need? throw low now

rows.name: Basic rules
rows.author: Yosif Elessawi
rows.description: Follows a short list of rules a person wrote.
method: bid the tricks the hand should win
still need tricks? win as cheaply as possible

rows.name: Random
rows.author: Yosif Elessawi
rows.description: Plays any legal move. It's the bottom of the scale.

rows.name: Claude Opus 5.5
rows.author: Essam Gouda
rows.description: Anthropic's general AI model, not built for this game. For each move it reads the rules and its own view of the table in words, then picks one. It has no tools and remembers nothing between moves.
method: put the rules and this seat's view into words
Claude thinks it over and picks a move
